model_annotation: The plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several language model variants, comparing their convergence behavior. The x-axis represents the number of iterations, ranging from 0 to 140,000 on a linear scale, with tick marks spaced every 20,000 iterations. The y-axis represents the loss, ranging from 2.4 to 3.4 on a linear scale, with tick marks every 0.1 unit. Five lines are shown: a purple dashed line labeled "Vanilla," a blue solid line labeled "StrmLLM (n=64)," an orange solid line labeled "SepLLM (n=64)," a green solid line labeled "SepLLM (n=64, H)," a red solid line labeled "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)," and a dark blue solid line labeled "SepLLM (n=128)." All lines start near a loss of 3.4 at iteration 0 and exhibit a steep decline in the initial phase, followed by a gradual decrease toward convergence. The "Vanilla" model (purple) achieves the lowest loss, stabilizing around 2.5 by 140,000 iterations. The "StrmLLM (n=64)" (blue) shows the highest loss throughout, stabilizing near 2.6. The "SepLLM (n=64)" (orange) and "SepLLM (n=64, H)" (green) converge to similar losses around 2.52–2.53. The "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" (red) and "SepLLM (n=128)" (dark blue) converge to slightly lower losses, around 2.51–2.52, with the latter showing the most consistent decline. All lines exhibit some noise, particularly in the early iterations, but overall trends are smooth and downward.
